Backend Expectations

Current backend truth:

  • SystemVerilog: primary live backend
  • Verilog: supported through the existing path
  • VHDL: bounded direct single-FSM and exact composition subsets are shipped; full-backend parity and external compiler qualification remain backlog

For a supported root, --language vhdl routes through the live VHDL backend. Unsupported expressions, declarations, generic maps, aggregate shapes, packages, or composition forms fail closed instead of silently falling back to SystemVerilog. Text generation alone is not external qualification: this environment has no GHDL or equivalent VHDL compiler lane. The exact shipped matrix and remaining full-backend work are canonical under Backends And Validation.

Composition VHDL is intentionally exact rather than general. The shipped families cover the documented C1 standalone-DT, C2 generated-FSM, C3 external- RTL, and APB/C4 generated-FSM fixtures; other composition shapes are rejected before HDL emission with an explicit target-support diagnostic.

Explicitly Out Of Active Support

FSMGen should fail closed when a source uses syntax outside the active contract. Current out-of-support examples include:

  • malformed +system sections, including duplicate clock/reset entries, malformed clock/reset identifiers, and missing clock declarations
  • unsupported top-level directive sections such as (+clock clk), (+areset rst_n), or (+bogus ...)
  • unsupported tagged wrappers such as ?define:legacy_template and other template roots outside the active ?fsm, ?dt, ?mod, ?module, and ?top families
  • historical template files such as fsm/generic_fifo.fsm, whose ?define:generic_fifo root, ?&generic_fifo macro instantiations, bracket placeholders, and ?repeat forms remain outside the active parser contract
  • bare top-level FSM content without a supported source root
  • unsupported top-level FSM body forms inside a supported root, such as (tester_reset := 1) or (BROKEN 1)
  • bare condition suffixes such as (A <= B start) and (-> busy full)
  • empty guarded blocks such as (<req) or malformed action-only forms such as (BROKEN)
  • malformed state/DT blocks that carry no real body, such as (idle) or (-misc)
  • malformed selector branches without actions, such as (?MODE (=0))
  • bare selector labels such as (?MODE (BUSY ...)) or (?MODE (0 ...))
  • duplicate default selector branches in the same selector node, such as (default ...) together with (_ ...)
  • computed test nodes without a selector expression or without branches, such as (? (=0 ...)) or (?(| A B))
  • unsupported expression operators, malformed operator arity, or guard-only tokens in ordinary RHS expression position
  • malformed delayed-pulse assignments with non-literal RHS values or unsupported indexed, sliced, aggregate, or deconstruct LHS targets
  • legacy composition/template forms such as ?&..., nested ?top, nested ?ports mapping directives, nested ?wiring, multi-source ?fsmc, placeholder selectors, repeat macros, and placeholder tokens
  • composition requests with no child instances, empty child entries, non-string child headers, dotted-pair child payloads, duplicate child names, duplicate top ports, unsupported child kinds, legacy ?ports mapping directives, multiple ?ports blocks, omitted or empty ?ports outside inferable lanes, missing explicit ?wiring for explicit-link topologies, C1 passthrough missing exposure, unknown top-port, width mismatch, or direction mismatch failures, declared same-name on shared system ports, aggregate-member child endpoints without declared aggregate types, malformed verbose ?ports declarations, invalid ?ports tokens, non-positive ?ports widths, malformed ?wiring list-form endpoints, unsupported ?wiring tokens, strict-mode legacy ?wiring /source/target/ slash-link tokens, malformed composition-top symbol names, or non-literal composition-top enum values, missing external generated child sources, wrong-kind external generated-child roots such as ?fsmc resolving to ?dt:name or ?dtc resolving to ?fsm:name, malformed ?fsmc / ?dtc source counts, unsupported nested ?fsmc / ?dtc payload blocks, malformed ?rtl module-reference counts, unsupported nested ?rtl payload blocks, or external RTL metadata that is missing, non-flat, empty, duplicated, wrongly typed, or system-output directed

This list is not a replacement for the exact diagnostic text. It is the book home for the active rejection policy: unsupported syntax should be rejected with local context instead of being interpreted opportunistically.

Practical Debug Checklist

  1. Re-run with trace enabled.
  2. Confirm the active root kind.
  3. Confirm imported packages and search roots.
  4. Confirm port widths and directions.
  5. Confirm named type compatibility when aliases are involved.
  6. Inspect generated HDL or structural IR if planning succeeded.

Regression Guidance

Before landing behavior changes, run the local regression suite:

./bin/ci-regression quick
./bin/ci-regression smoke
./bin/ci-regression isf
./bin/ci-regression vial-gate
./bin/ci-regression

Use quick for a small smoke set when you need fast feedback on basic direct .fsm, composition, and ISF functionality. smoke is an alias for the same tier. Use isf for the current ISF-focused 109x, 11xx, 12xx, and 13xx numbered bands. Use vial-gate only for the selected authenticated architecture- scale gate. With no mode argument, ./bin/ci-regression runs the full Perl suite, then that VIAL gate, and remains the unsharded pre-push gate.

For focused work, run the nearby targeted prove suites first, then the smallest ci-regression tier that covers the changed surface. The gate builds the mdBook by default, so generated docs and runtime behavior stay under the same local quality check. Use --list to inspect the concrete quick/ISF test sets and --no-book only for a deliberately code-only turnaround check.

GitHub Actions is active under .github/workflows/. The hosted regression workflow runs the same ./bin/ci-regression entrypoint on pushes to main, pull requests targeting main, and manual runs. Hosted execution uses 16 disjoint ordinary-file shards, five dedicated long/provider-dependent tests, 16 entry shards for each of four supported-corpus audits, and one isolated job for each of the 68 cases in the large dynamic transaction-ID focused test. All four Perl matrices continue after individual failures. A final required result succeeds only when every shard, doctrine enforcement, the separate mdBook build, and one unsharded VIAL regression-promotion gate succeed. Exactly the dedicated t/1598, t/1648, and t/1650 coordinates materialize exact OSVVM 2026.05 beneath their isolated repository- local caches; only t/1436 receives its pinned HDL tools. Hosted shards do not inherit the local VIAL gate lifecycle. The ordinary local ./bin/ci-regression command remains unsharded and includes both that lifecycle and the book build. The separate hosted gate pins Ubuntu 24.04 and Perl 5.32, rejects ambient Verilator or the fixed GHDL coordinates, materializes exact OSVVM 2026.05, calls ./bin/ci-regression vial-gate --no-book, and independently authenticates the expected eight-informational/three-unavailable latest result before an always-running cleanup removes its owned evidence, provider, result, and stage. This is configured CI coverage; independent execution closeout remains a separate step and no hosted performance or support claim follows from it. The GitHub Pages workflow builds this mdBook from docs/book and publishes the generated docs/book/book artifact when Pages is configured to use GitHub Actions.

Hosted regression uses a minimal Perl setup. Ordinary runtime paths should not depend on undeclared local CPAN modules, and CLI report modes that are tested for clean stderr must remain compatible with the hosted Perl version.

Guarded commands and standard input

Keep diagnostic logs and captured native/compiler evidence when maintaining generated artifacts. Periodic cleanup removes only proven obsolete renders or duplicate replay source/index views authenticated against immutable Git bytes and complete public index membership. The current book, committed sources and original audit evidence remain available. Inspection rejects tracked candidates, symlink parents, shared hard links, foreign volumes and nested repositories before removing a fixed target. Cache views may be regenerated by legitimate replay; saved cleanup receipts prove dated removal and preservation, rather than promising future absence or identical binary index metadata. A sweep with no proven disposable candidate retains all artifacts and records that result. docs/ARTIFACT_CLEANUP.md records the latest repository-owned sweep. Rust sweeps inspect release, incremental and dependency directories for .bin and .log files; retained evidence is recorded separately from disposable candidates.

The repository RAM guard preserves standard input for the command it supervises. Pipes, input files and interpreter programs supplied on stdin therefore work:

printf '%s\n' 'print "guarded stdin\n";' | scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -

The command prints guarded stdin. Guard diagnostics go to standard error, and the command’s exit status is preserved. The memory cutoffs remain 88% of host occupied capacity and 4096 MiB RSS per descendant. A cutoff stops the command tree and returns the guard’s documented failure status.

Earlier guard versions discarded stdin when launching their background child. A program supplied on stdin could consequently exit zero without executing. The regression retains that exact committed version as an independent failure control, and verifies binary pipe/file bytes, EOF, nonzero child exit and a separate inherited descriptor alongside the existing cutoff and cleanup tests:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl \
  t/2011-ram-guard-stdin.t t/1595-agent-runtime-ram-guard-macos-metric.t \
  t/1811-ram-guard-fixture-runtime.t

Decision-store diagnostics

Maintainers can audit decision identities and consumer references at a fixed source revision without moving records or changing their authority:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- python3 -B scripts/audit_decision_identity_capacity.py \
  --revision 25c01f0127144922ade78951b91439e1d9221c08 \
  > .artifacts/decision-identity-capacity.json

The JSON names its source revision, exact index destinations, record digests, sealed-reader comparisons, root dimensions and scoped consumer candidates. It runs the captured reader in a repository-local temporary fixture. Basename and literal-fragment searches include tracked provenance; generic code-path candidates are listed separately. This is historical evidence, with explicit limits for dynamic and external consumers. It does not move decision records or replace their current discovery index.

The decision rollover also has separately qualified catalog and authenticated store preparation modules. Maintainers can exercise their literal future-store fixtures:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl \
  t/2000-decision-catalog-preparation.t t/2001-decision-store-navigation.t

These controls check source/original identity, semantic routes, copied metadata, record bytes and unsafe or missing files. Store controls also authenticate the transition source and original index, preserve compatibility headings, and check complete root/part navigation against selected bytes. Production now uses this authenticated store, while the old sealed-reader behavior remains available for historical snapshots without a catalog.

The published reader also handles explicitly supplied authenticated stores. Such a store requires --root, --source-sha256 and --index-sha256; the digests must come from independent trusted source/index evidence. The current repository installs its own fixed transition pins. Without a catalog, ordinary check and sealed read retain their existing behavior.

OperationSelected product
read IDsCaptured original bytes when available; current bytes for fresh uncaptured IDs.
read-original IDsCaptured originals; an uncaptured fresh ID refuses.
read-current IDsCurrent canonical bodies in an authenticated store; sealed-only IDs refuse.
resolve CANONICAL_PATHExact authenticated canonical ID/path/source/content binding; this grants no new authority.

Requests validate completely before any record output. Current owned status or first-time fact-index changes preserve immutable original products. Malformed schema kinds, missing or altered store products and unavailable IDs refuse. Exercise the actual CLI controls with:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2002-decision-reader-stores.t

Selected Git access and prior/current catalog continuity also have independent controls:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2003-decision-store-git-continuity.t

They pin selected object IDs rather than borrowing later index/worktree data, and reject deletion/reuse of decision identities or loss of previously published fact/question keys. The gate enforces this comparison on every catalog change; standalone current validation cannot infer records born after its fixed source census.

The published operations can select --snapshot index, HEAD, HEAD^ or an exact Git commit; omitted selection uses the working files. Selected reads use the captured regular blobs and complete root inventory throughout, including legacy sealed-record checks. Later working edits cannot supply missing selected bytes or replace selected navigation.

The complete selected path/mode/object inventory is limited by its existing 4-MiB metadata byte budget. Its entry bound follows the minimum Git record size, so unrelated tracked evidence does not hit a separate fixed file-count limit. Byte overflow still refuses before any selected product is published; conflicting stages, nonregular sources and missing selected blobs also refuse. The continuity test exercises actual index and committed-tree growth beyond the former count limit, followed by actual byte overflow.

check-continuity additionally requires --prior-snapshot HEAD, HEAD^ or an exact commit. It returns one bounded JSON product after authenticating both selected stores. Optional canonical path arguments return exact bindings, current text and fresh_identity, which is relative to the selected predecessor. A record born after the transition is fresh once; a later check against its published predecessor returns false. This binding alone grants no ceiling increase. For an explicitly trusted fixture store:

scripts/decision_records.py --root "$store_root" \
  --source-sha256 "$trusted_source_sha256" --index-sha256 "$trusted_index_sha256" \
  --snapshot index --prior-snapshot HEAD check-continuity

The fingerprints must come from independent trusted evidence. Supplying them for the reader’s own repository is refused, including when production pins are installed. First catalog adoption must match the exact predecessor commit, complete root identity population, original index and original bodies. Catalog removal, lost prior IDs or question/fact keys, invalid requests and oversized change products refuse without partial output. With neither snapshot containing a catalog, the change product reports catalog: false; it makes no sealed-reader qualification claim. The Perl ceiling-authority gate now consumes the same atomic product whenever either selected snapshot has a catalog.

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2004-decision-reader-snapshots.t

The ceiling-authority gate selects staged, working or committed changes from the controlled decision store and reader inputs as well as registry/authority files. Ordinary catalog growth or updates receive prior-current continuity checks even when no ceiling increases. Existing flat historical authorities remain append-only, and no-catalog controls retain their legacy behavior.

Canonical authority additionally requires a fresh decision ID, a canonical file absent from the selected predecessor, and the four exact authority markers outside fenced examples. A relocated transition record or a previously published birth cannot authorize a new increase. Mixed staged/working controlled files, malformed stores, lost identities and mismatched control-file bytes refuse. The reader’s optional --bind-file PATH arguments expose selected prior/current SHA-256 bindings; the gate uses these to compare its registry and authority bytes with the same captured reader inventory. Output and diagnostics are bounded.

The actual gate accepts independently trusted fixture fingerprints only with an explicit other --root. They cannot override production authority at its own repository root. Boolean schema versions refuse in both registry metadata and authority rows. Production catalog delivery and pins use the qualified atomic rollover; this integration does not raise a ceiling.

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2005-decision-ceiling-stores.t

Post-transition facts also have an independent mode matrix. Its complete current snapshots pass standalone authentication and navigation before the actual prior comparison rejects identity/path/type recycling, lost facts/questions and reused earlier ID gaps. Additive owned content/status/summary/question changes pass.

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2006-decision-identity-modes.t

Malformed source/original/catalog products, missing navigation rows, altered compatibility pages and unsafe files refuse in every selected gate mode. Orphan, reused, borrowed and misrouted authority also refuses. Installed default mode additionally preserves the published sealed originals; fixture pins cannot replace that authority. Supplied fingerprints must have the required lowercase hexadecimal form even when neither selected snapshot has a catalog. A valid no-catalog request retains its explicit non-catalog result.

The controlled reader-dispatch tests also plant oversized output and diagnostics, malformed JSON products and signal failure after valid output. Each refuses:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2007-decision-hostile-boundaries.t

Production current bodies live below docs/decisions/current/, grouped into continuity, language/API and verification indexes. The complete decision index links directly to each body. Old root paths retain the original heading sequence and point to the complete record; add future records to a current part and its catalog, rather than extending the fixed compatibility population.

Captured originals and current owned rendering are separate products:

scripts/decision_records.py read-original 0113
scripts/decision_records.py read-current 0113
scripts/decision_records.py check
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2008-decision-production-rollover.t

The immutable transition census, original bodies and original index bind to an exact preceding Git commit. Production pins authenticate that evidence, and the initial adoption gate compares the complete predecessor population and bytes. The historical capacity audit above remains a historical selection record; current storage checks use the delivered authenticated store.

The fixed production relocation also has an independent consumer-continuity audit. It compares complete Knowledge Map question/fact/path bindings and authored inline destinations, checks every original heading forwarder, and lists full-basename references separately from generic code candidates:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- python3 -B scripts/audit_decision_store_consumer_closure.py \
  --revision df7f692c8b94b083d2d078d62854d37869fbca6d \
  > .artifacts/decision-consumer-closure.json
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/2009-decision-consumer-closure.t

Stable exported provenance identifiers retain their published paths. Current body readers follow the canonical records. The controls plant lost/substituted question bindings and wrong heading/relative destinations. This proof covers the named tracked source cohort; it does not enumerate dynamic or external consumers or execute HDL. Fresh-record growth is qualified separately below.

Successful fresh growth also has a complete production-cohort fixture:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -v -Iperl t/2010-decision-production-growth.t

It copies fixed committed store products and their declared archive destinations, retains the installed independent pins, and publishes a fixture predecessor before adding a literal fact-bearing record. Actual original/current retrieval and prior-aware Perl admission pass working, staged and committed selections. Physical current membership gains the record while compatibility aliases remain fixed. Python and Perl independently measure capacity under unchanged ceilings; the fixture declares its resulting aggregate warning pressure. The literal lives only in the isolated qualification workspace.

The same complete cohort also qualifies malformed-product refusal:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -v -Iperl t/2012-decision-production-hostile.t

The fixture first publishes an authenticated birth, then independently removes or changes a compatibility heading, duplicates or misroutes root/part navigation, and changes or removes the current body. The actual public check, current retrieval, prior-continuity operation and Perl authority gate refuse each selected working, staged and committed product. Public failures emit no partial record. Each case restores the exact valid fixture publication, and immutable originals, independent pins, control products and enforcement ceilings remain fixed. Published identity and question floors also have a complete production-cohort matrix:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -v -Iperl t/2013-decision-production-floors.t

Each isolated fixture publishes its authored fact and questions before testing identity deletion/replacement, path/type recycling, fact loss/substitution and question loss/substitution. Descriptors and all navigation routes are updated consistently, so current authentication passes first. The actual prior-aware public operation and Perl gate then reject each loss in working, staged and committed selections. Counts that stay equal do not excuse replaced identities or keys. Owned content, status and additive questions pass the same modes. These fixtures preserve installed independent pins, immutable originals and enforcement ceilings; their warning pressure is declared without publishing fictional ADRs.

Together these source-bound qualifications close the decision-store rollover prerequisite under SEM .51. Record-input frontend/public qualification resumes under .60.4.3.2.3.6; generated/domain carriers and native/consumer completion retain separate owners. The canonical SPECFORGE response records the reset answer and remaining feature deliveries.

Current Boundary

The project is trying to move toward:

  • early failure
  • local diagnostics
  • regression-locked contracts

If a failure feels vague or misleading, that is still a product-quality gap, not something users should simply accept.

FSMGen Book

Extensions and Embedding

This chapter covers the current supported integration seam for tool builders.

Working directories and legacy search initialization

The legacy PathSearch helper retains its installed tree when loaded through a relative Perl include path before the caller changes directory. Directory enumeration stays lazy: the first nonempty search includes the caller’s directory at that time. Explicit extra directories remain available to subsequent searches; default .conf extensions and missing-file warnings keep their existing meaning. This does not change ISF library search precedence or introduce a new public API.

Capability Manifest Discovery

The machine-readable entrypoint for downstream tools is:

./bin/fsmgen --capability-manifest

The top-level manifest_contract object owns the bounded shell for that JSON.

It now also publishes a grouped top_level_contract_source_map for the public top-level sections:

  • producer
  • support_accounting
  • diagnostics
  • semantic_exports
  • backend_validation
  • embedding
  • language_surface
  • verification_outputs
  • documentation

That grouped map is the intended discovery surface for embedders.

It lets a tool start from one manifest object, then hand each public top-level section to its dedicated contract owner without reconstructing the owner map from scattered section payloads, hard-coding owner strings, or remembering that language_surface still advertises its nested owner under surface_contract for compatibility.

The same manifest shell now also publishes a grouped top_level_section_presence_key_map so a downstream tool can discover the bounded key family for each public top-level section from one place instead of collecting those section-key lists field by field.

For verification_outputs, that family is the exact live section payload: the target/artifact/validation discovery fields, section_contract, guidance, and json_safe_when_embedded_in_public_manifest are all present in both the grouped manifest map and the section’s own public_top_level_presence_keys. Consumers do not need an undocumented payload-key exception.

It now also publishes a grouped presence_key_family_map so a downstream tool can discover the manifest-owned legacy *_presence_keys field families from one place instead of collecting those compatibility field lists one by one.

The language_surface.file_surfaces section advertises the shipped public file suffixes: .fsm as IAL0, .isf as IAL1, .ppif as the generic IAL2 container, and the bounded profile aliases .axi, .apb, and .ahb. These IAL2 surfaces lower through generated .isf before generated .fsm and publish their supported CLI modes, including --emit-schedule-json, --check-json, and --emit-semantic-json. Historical or future spellings .pif, .ppi, .chi, .ace, .atb, .smbus, and .i2s remain outside the bounded public surface.

The same manifest boundary now describes the current IAL2 contract for any downstream consumer: bounded public .ppif covers one-channel Valid-Ready sources, multi-channel Valid-Ready bundles, one-object AXI manager capacity/status sources, APB requester-transfer sources, APB completer sources, fixed one-requester/one-completer APB composition sources, and their selected busy-capable and status-capable APB variants. Bounded .axi aliases currently cover the selected AXI Valid-Ready surface, and bounded .apb aliases cover selected APB requester-transfer, completer, fixed composition, busy-capable APB sources, and busy-gated 2-bit status APB sources. Bounded .ahb aliases currently cover the selected AHB requester surface. Support-accounted AXI manager coverage includes capacity/status, ID-family metadata, transaction envelopes and fan-in, concrete-ID assertions, bounded auto-ID lifecycle, same-ID reject and issue-order-queue policy, generated auto-ID write/read response-demux, generated single/last/multi-beat read-data capture, burst-length/runtime validation, scalar RRESP aggregation, one-or-more read burst-last queue-head groups, one-or-more write queue-head groups, read single-beat and read burst-last queue-head response-demux including multiple/mixed depth-3 scalar, raw-ARLEN, runtime-validation, and multi-beat output-bank read-data groups, same-family mixed auto-ID plus concrete queue-head response-demux with scalar, raw-ARLEN, runtime-validation, and multi-beat output-bank read-data over the selected read burst-last shape, generated single-active and multiple all-dynamic write/read response-demux, generated all-dynamic same-ID issue-order queues for selected write BID, read single-beat RID, and read burst-last RID && RLAST depth-2/depth-3 shapes, selected read-data, raw-ARLEN, runtime-validation, and multi-beat output-bank behavior over generated all-dynamic read burst-last issue-order queues, generated mixed dynamic/static response-demux families, generated one-dynamic plus one-concrete-static mixed dynamic/static same-ID issue-order queue behavior for write BID, read single-beat RID, and read burst-last RID && RLAST, generated one-dynamic plus two-concrete-static mixed dynamic/static write BID same-ID issue-order queue behavior, paired scalar read-data over the generated mixed read single-beat and burst-last queue completions, report-only raw-ARLEN burst-length capture, runtime beat-count/RLAST validation, and runtime-validation multi-beat output banks over the generated mixed read burst-last queue completion. Broader mixed issue-order queue cardinality beyond that selected write BID multi-static shape, scoreboards, group-local simultaneous enqueue widening, packed burst-vector outputs, alternate full burst payload assembly, aliases, platform clauses, full AXI manager behavior, direct backend lowering, verification-output generation, backend-language variants, and VHDL remain deferred. This manifest boundary, the downstream handoff, the public contracts, this book, support-accounting, and the codebase must remain lockstep.

The embedding section’s serializable_plan_reports branch also advertises public_top_level_presence_keys and json_safe_surface_keys; both the standalone parent contract and the manifest-embedded branch are JSON-round-trip audited so embedders can validate the bounded shell, confirm its identity metadata, discover the advertised portable report surfaces they decoded, and check the public key lists for the bounded shell itself and for the normalized semantic and composition provenance reports those surfaces point at.

The same manifest section also advertises embedding.serializable_generation_result_snapshot directly so embedders can discover the JSON-safe HDLGenerator result summary contract without traversing the broader plan/report branch. The existing embedding.serializable_plan_reports.generation_result_snapshot_contract reference remains in place for plan/report compatibility.

A matching defensive-copy guard proves caller mutation of the parent public-key list does not pollute the next built contract, and the JSON-safe surface list has the same focused mutation guard.

The parent surface-to-owner map is also defensively rebuilt, so callers cannot mutate one decoded contract into the next.

The same parent branch embeds the composition-plan snapshot child contract, and that embedded child contract is JSON-round-trip audited against its canonical owner and defensively rebuilt after caller mutation.

Current Philosophy

The active extension model is typed and explicit.

A typed extension is a normal blessed Perl object with explicit hook methods.

The hook receives a typed context object with named accessors such as source_info, target_language, raw_ast, and result.

Before dispatch, the active pipeline validates that configured extension entries are blessed objects with at least one real supported hook method.

It is not:

  • legacy .plg discovery
  • implicit hook-name lookup
  • stringly plugin callbacks
  • AUTOLOAD hook discovery
  • implicit CLI plugin discovery

It is:

  • explicit Perl modules
  • explicit hook methods
  • typed context objects
  • explicit programmatic or CLI loading

For backend-language portability, this is a bounded Perl reference surface, not a portable plugin API. BACKEND-LANGUAGE-PORTABILITY-CONTRACT-FRONTIER.2.7 selects typed extension/plugin support as out of scope for the first non-Perl implementation experiment unless a future exact task first selects a portable extension API. A non-Perl variant that does not implement that future API must advertise extension support as unsupported and fail closed on extension loading requests.

Typed Extensions

Current shipped hooks are:

  • after_parse_source($context)
  • after_generate_result($context)

These run:

  • after parsed-source classification
  • after normal generation result assembly

This hook/context boundary is now advertised in the capability manifest under embedding.typed_extensions, owned by FSM::Support::ExtensionContract.

That machine-readable contract records:

  • explicit object/module/config loading entrypoints
  • the shipped hook names
  • the stable context accessor names
  • the rule that extension modules loaded by name must provide a real new() method
  • the rule that registry extension arrays are copied while extension objects remain live hook objects
  • and the deliberate absence of legacy .plg discovery, automatic directory discovery, and AUTOLOAD hook dispatch

That registry ownership rule is runtime-audited directly: mutating the caller’s extension array after FSM::Extension::Registry->new(...), or mutating an extensions() accessor array, cannot add hooks to the registry.

The extension objects themselves remain live hook objects by identity.

The same construction-time ownership applies at the facade loader entrypoint: HDLGenerator->new(extension_modules => \@modules) resolves and registers the listed modules during construction, so later caller mutation of @modules does not add, remove, or replace hooks on that facade object.

HDLGenerator->new(extension_config_files => \@configs) follows the same rule for config-file discovery: the constructor-time config path list is read during facade construction, and later caller mutation of @configs cannot change the installed hooks.

Direct HDLGenerator->new(extensions => \@objects) construction follows the registry rule as well: the array container is snapped at construction, while the extension objects themselves remain live hook objects by identity.

That same owner now also publishes a grouped name_family_map so embedders can discover the bounded hook-name, context-accessor, and supported-source-kind families from one place instead of collecting those name lists separately.

That grouped discovery key is itself now listed in the contract’s advertised top-level key list, and t/306-extension-contract.t checks that the typed-extension contract’s advertised top-level keys cover the exact emitted contract shell.

The current context accessors are:

  • stage
  • pipeline
  • source_path
  • target_language
  • source_info
  • raw_ast
  • result

source_info->{kind} is the classified root kind, such as fsm, dt, or composition.

source_info and raw_ast accessors return fresh snapshots; mutating them does not alter the stored context.

raw_ast is available on after_parse_source.

result is available on after_generate_result and remains the live result hash.

Reusable HDLGenerator facade objects build new extension context snapshots for each generation, so mutations to one hook invocation’s source_info or raw_ast snapshots do not leak into later hook invocations on the same facade.

Result augmentation is a valid in-process extension use, but it is not the same thing as publishing a new sanitized JSON interchange field.

t/379-extension-result-json-boundary-audit.t locks that split: extension-added raw result fields and HDL text remain available to in-process callers, while --emit-semantic-json and FSM::Support::NormalizedSemanticReport keep them out of the public JSON payload.

Programmatic Example

use FSM::Pipeline::HDLGenerator;

{
    package My::ResultMarker;

    sub new { bless {}, shift }

    sub after_generate_result {
        my ($self, $context) = @_;
        $context->result->{extension_marker} = {
            source_kind => $context->source_info->{kind},
            target_language => $context->target_language,
        };
    }
}

my $pipeline = FSM::Pipeline::HDLGenerator->new(
    target_language => 'systemverilog',
    extensions => [ My::ResultMarker->new ],
);

my $result = $pipeline->generate_hdl_from_file('fsm/trial_0.fsm');

For in-process embedders, FSM::Pipeline::HDLGenerator no longer leaves its requested debug_level behind as process-global state after construction or generation.

The pipeline now scopes its debug setting to the constructor or generation call and restores the caller’s prior FSM::Debug state afterward.

If an embedder needs to rebind tracing manually, the current shipped save/restore seam is:

use FSM::Debug qw(
    capture_fsm_debug_state
    restore_fsm_debug_state
    set_fsm_trace_output_file
    set_fsm_trace_verbosity
);

my $saved = capture_fsm_debug_state();
set_fsm_trace_output_file('embedded-trace.log');
set_fsm_trace_verbosity('debug');

# ... temporary embedded tracing work ...

restore_fsm_debug_state($saved);

That restore path preserves the caller-facing trace/debug configuration, including the original trace sink, instead of forcing embedders to reconstruct global debug state by hand after a temporary trace-file switch.

For CLI loading, the module must already be available in Perl’s @INC, for example through PERL5LIB, and it must provide a real new() constructor.

PERL5LIB=./my_extensions ./bin/fsmgen \
  --extension-module My::ResultMarker \
  --output .artifacts/sv/trial_0-extension.sv \
  fsm/trial_0.fsm

Config-file loading is also explicit.

The config file lists module names, and those modules must also already be available in @INC with real new() constructors:

module My::ResultMarker

PERL5LIB=./my_extensions ./bin/fsmgen \
  --extension-config extensions.fsmext \
  --output .artifacts/sv/trial_0-extension.sv \
  fsm/trial_0.fsm

Do not treat the raw HDLGenerator result hash as a stable JSON document.

Some nested branches still contain live CoreAST/AST objects for compatibility and in-process tooling.

If you need sanitized machine interchange, use --emit-semantic-json or the FSM::Support::NormalizedSemanticReport surface instead.

Composition provenance has one more important split:

  • raw fsm_module is a live CoreAST object and is not a public JSON API
  • raw raw_ast is a parser/debug artifact and is not a public interchange API
  • raw composition_spec is a live parsed composition object and is not a public JSON API
  • raw composition_report is useful for in-process Perl tooling, but it can still contain private live objects in nested endpoint contexts
  • raw composition_plan is a live planning object and is not a public JSON API
  • normalized semantic JSON exposes the sanitized semantic.composition.provenance_report fragment for downstream tools

That fragment preserves bounded public report facts such as the composition lane, top-port and resolved-link counts, provenance origin counts, ordered origin/kind lists, ports, resolved links, override events, and block events, while stripping private Perl objects before JSON emission.

On the current live path, structural_rtl_ir instance bindings are not just flat signal names anymore.

They can preserve:

  • connection_expr for the structural source shape
  • connection_type_name when a binding reuses a declared named type alias
  • connection_type_spec when the planner already knows the typed signal, expression, or whole-aggregate actual contract

That means embedding tools can inspect whether a binding came from a plain typed signal, an inferred list-like concat/repeat expression, or a whole aggregate actual root without reconstructing that meaning from packed width alone.

Composition provenance endpoint contexts also preserve typed aggregate source expression facts.

For example, in_frame.tag and producer.OUT_FRAME.payload[1] report the resolved aggregate leaf width/type when their base endpoint carries a declared aggregate type, rather than forcing embedders to infer that path from string spelling or whole-base widths.

On the composition side, module_info.composition_shared_datapath_candidates also now preserves declared type contracts conservatively:

  • width-equal typed child-output families do not collapse into one candidate when their declared type contracts disagree
  • uniform typed shared-datapath families preserve one candidate-level declared type contract
  • and the raw contributor nets synthesized during shared-datapath lifting keep contributor-side declared type identity in the structural export
  • lifted shared runtime carriers such as *_shared_q, *_shared_next, and *_shared_comb now also live in that structural net surface with an explicit declaration kind instead of existing only as declaration text in auxiliary HDL sections

That is already useful for downstream tooling while the long-term public embedding/API stabilization lane (R13) is active but not fully frozen yet.

Important Boundary

Today, programmatic embedding exists, but it is not yet declared a fully frozen public API.

That means:

  • useful now for internal tooling and serious integration work
  • not yet promised as a permanently stable contract forever

The active R13 lane is where that public stabilization work is being graduated from useful internal seams into deliberate public contracts.

The fully frozen embedding API item is tracked in Feature Backlog.

bin/fsmgen-mcp is the first shipped read-only local JSON-RPC stdio adapter over this contract. Static resources expose capabilities, contracts, diagnostics, support accounting, examples, and catalog-backed source discovery. Source-bound resources/tools require a caller-approved workspace root and a source identity under that root; source-bound responses include adapter_provenance. Hardware reports normalize workspace/repo absolute paths and redact other absolute paths; VIAL uses its public relative-source result contract and preserves semantic paths. Protocol-level JSON-RPC failures use -32700 for parse errors, -32600 for invalid requests, -32601 for unknown methods, and -32000 for adapter call errors. Raw parser ASTs, private scheduler/lowering objects, HDLGenerator compatibility hashes, arbitrary shell output, network access, implicit file writes, write/generation tools, mutation workflows, and commit/push actions are not public semantic-introspection payloads.

Read-only MCP Workflow Examples

A generic local read-only client configuration uses the adapter command and an explicit workspace root:

{
  "command": "perl",
  "args": [
    "/path/to/fsmgen/bin/fsmgen-mcp",
    "--workspace-root",
    "/path/to/workspace"
  ]
}

Those workflows cover tool discovery, bounded support-accounting coverage, capability-contract queries, catalog-backed source discovery, example discovery, stable diagnostic explanation, strict check JSON, source-bound semantic inspection, and schedule previews. Source discovery returns only repo/workspace-relative catalog identities with file kind, source kind, available read-only query kinds, and support metadata; it does not traverse the workspace. The source-bound requests return workspace-relative source identity and adapter_provenance; they do not return the configured workspace root.

Generated DT-local and grouped assignment enables use one deterministic namespace per module. Case-distinct signals such as OUT and out retain independent conditions and write selection even when their readable enable names would coincide. Authored signals, system ports, parameters and top-level enable names are reserved; generated collisions receive numeric suffixes. Clients should use assignment_records[].provenance to identify the original signal, RHS and DT, not infer those identities by splitting generated names. CLI semantic reports and MCP expose the same repaired producer.

Use file_kind: "axi" or "ahb" for the other supported aliases. Discovery keeps catalog order, support identity, filtering and bounded limits; it does not scan arbitrary workspace directories or expose hidden/absolute paths.

Source checking, normalized hardware semantics and scheduling answer different questions. Use the public report that retains the authored information:

VIAL Semantic Queries and Version Selection

For .vial sources, fsmgen_check and fsmgen_semantic_introspect call the public FSM::VIAL::Tool::check_vial_source_file API. Both return the complete native check result under report, including semantic_report, source identities, capability/support evidence and structured diagnostics. The MCP query kind stays explicit, while native report.action remains check. No planning, backend execution or artifact publication occurs.

This VIAL report is a summary: it omits expression/action bodies and retains lifecycle family identity, revision and node count rather than node conditions, deadlines or service policies. Matching native and MCP summaries proves that transport preserves the report, not that an agent can inspect those details. The public typed source-inspection API and native vial inspect command supply those details. MCP exposes them through the dedicated fsmgen_vial_inspect tool and versioned inspection resource.

The public typed projection covers base source meaning and lifecycle_control@1: it retains declaration bodies, expressions, nested actions, source locations, exact model/fault scope and complete lifecycle nodes. Its independent record definitions are in the source-inspection contract. Lifecycle detail preserves readiness prerequisites, all service conditions, intrinsic and added dependencies, inclusive deadlines and failure cleanup policy. Deadline and cleanup bounds appear as typed cycle counts. Current MCP summary queries have not gained those bodies. Unknown family revisions and incomplete records cause projection refusal. The projection recovers authored declaration order from source locations. Native check and MCP summaries also preserve authored order after recursive type resolution. For example, (type first (type later)) (type later (u 8)) reports first,later, with each array position matching its semantic path. Cached semantic and compatibility digests for sources affected by the former dependency-first ordering require refreshing; canonical base fixture reports remain unchanged.

Service start requirements now check and plan correctly. For example, adding (start_requires (reset_inactive bus)) after (target fixture_background) retains configured status and declared dependencies, then adds the reset condition with its domain identity. Typed inspection preserves that complete conjunction. Canonical check and planning reports remain unchanged by the fix.

A lifecycle may use (dependencies) and (services) with (readiness ready). Its readiness condition then explicitly retains the configured entry precondition, with no invented dependency or service identity. This has the same meaning as adding (requires (configured)); authored (requires (all)) remains invalid. Existing nonempty readiness conditions and their order remain unchanged.

Inspect the complete lifecycle source from the repository root:

./bin/fsmgen vial inspect --json --language-version 2 vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial

Inspection requires --json and accepts only one relative source, the version selector and optional --style auto|normal|terse. Planning, runtime, publication and quiet options are rejected. Success exits zero; source, limit or projection refusal exits one; invocation and host-path errors exit two. JSON failures keep the same inspection envelope and ordered public diagnostics.

Discover coverage with ./bin/fsmgen --capability-manifest, at semantic_introspection.contract_surface_map.vial_source_inspection.inspection_contract, or call exported FSM::VIAL::Tool::vial_source_inspection_capabilities() with no arguments. This separate contract names callable APIs, schemas, source styles, loading limits, base semantic groups and admitted intent families. It currently declares lifecycle_control@1 for VIAL v2 and no family for v1. Frozen vial capabilities records retain their existing action lists; they are not the discovery route for this independent inspection feature.

The equivalent public filesystem API is:

perl -Iperl -MFSM::VIAL::Tool=inspect_vial_source_file -MJSON::PP -e '
  my $r = inspect_vial_source_file({
    workspace_root => ".",
    source_id => "vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial",
    language_version => 2, source_style => "auto",
  });
  print JSON::PP->new->canonical->pretty->encode($r);
  exit($r->{success} ? 0 : 1);
'

The result uses fsmgen.vial_source_inspection.v1, independently of language version. check_result retains the complete existing native check. inspection.packages[].fixtures[].scenarios[].actions[] exposes authored actions; inspection.packages[].intent_families[].nodes[] exposes lifecycle conditions and policy. A deadline node has payload.detail.max_cycles, from, until and last_cycle_inclusive; service and failure nodes retain their corresponding typed conditions and cleanup policy.

An embedding host that already owns source bytes can avoid filesystem access:

use FSM::VIAL::Tool qw(inspect_vial_source);
my $result = inspect_vial_source({
    source_id => $relative_source_id, text => $source_bytes,
    source_catalog => $relative_import_ids_to_bytes,
    language_version => 2, source_style => 'auto',
});

Both calls require a closed invocation hash and return fresh JSON-safe values without printing, planning, running a backend or publishing artifacts. Omitted version selects v1; omitted style selects auto. The portable catalog defaults to empty. The filesystem adapter applies the same bounded root/import loader as source checking, captures each source once and never reopens it after check. Source failures retain the ordered native diagnostics and null inspection. If typed projection itself fails, outer success is false, detail is null, and VIAL_SOURCE_INSPECTION_ERROR contains a fixed public message; the successful native check remains intact. Always test the outer success flag.

Deep VIAL Inspection Through MCP

Query the independent capability contract, inspect the current lifecycle source, and read the equivalent versioned resource:

perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":31,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"fsmgen_capability_query","arguments":{"section":"vial_inspection"}}}'
perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":32,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"fsmgen_vial_inspect","arguments":{"source_id":"vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial","language_version":2}}}'
perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":33,"method":"resources/read","params":{"uri":"fsmgen://vial/2/source/vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial/inspection"}}'

The tool accepts only required relative source_id, optional language_version and optional source_style: auto|normal|terse. It has no source_path alias or absolute-path input. Omitted version selects v1 and omitted style selects auto; the resource always uses auto. tools/list, resource templates, capability manifest and VIAL source-discovery query kinds all advertise this route.

Both text JSON and structuredContent carry query_kind: inspection and the complete public result under report. Read report.inspection for typed detail and report.check_result for the complete source check. Tool isError follows the outer inspection success, including when checking succeeded but projection failed. Source/import/path failures retain native diagnostics and null detail; malformed arguments return JSON-RPC invalid params. Resource content preserves the same envelope. Public semantic paths retain their original identities.

For example, lifecycle service nodes retain authored start_requires conditions with their domain IDs; empty readiness retains its configured precondition; deadline and failure nodes expose inclusive bounds and cleanup policy. Base expressions, actions, model-instance and fault-binding identities remain typed. These queries use the public filesystem inspection API without planning, random evaluation, backend execution, publication or the hardware command runner.

JSON Transport Encoding

Both newline stdio and --request-json consume and emit UTF-8 JSON bytes. Literal Unicode and JSON Unicode escapes retain the same request identity and report values. Newline responses remain compact, with exactly one message per line; one-shot responses remain formatted. Tool text still carries the complete ASCII-escaped JSON payload alongside its equal structuredContent value.

For example, these calls return the same Unicode request identity:

printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"inspection-é","method":"ping"}' | perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root .
perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"inspection-é","method":"ping"}'

The outer transport uses UTF-8 encoding to avoid excessive temporary memory when escaping large embedded report text. Reports are neither truncated nor filtered to fit a test budget. The resource regression exercises both actual CLI modes with a large synthetic report, Unicode identities and typed values; the complete source-query cohort separately qualifies real feature reports. This removes the demonstrated encoding amplification, not the ordinary memory needed to construct, retain and transmit a complete report.

Feature Coverage Qualification

Feature coverage is selected from the public supported-source catalog and query applicability map. The test-side FSM::Test::SourceQueryCoverage helper retains every supported catalog ID with its family, coverage bucket, capability/phase metadata and nonclaims, while grouping shared physical sources. Hardware uses strict admission; VIAL source versions are explicitly registered and checked against the actual public fixtures. Unknown query/source mappings, unmapped or stale VIAL registrations, unsafe paths and conflicting shared-source metadata fail selection. Expected failures and legacy inputs remain separate populations.

For a focused, list-only view from the repository root:

perl -Iperl -It/lib -MFSM::Test::SourceQueryCoverage=build_source_query_cohort,select_source_query_cohort -MJSON::PP -e 'print JSON::PP->new->canonical->pretty->encode(select_source_query_cohort({cohort=>build_source_query_cohort(),source_ids=>["isf/storage_fields.isf","vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial"]}))'

Focus preserves catalog order and refuses empty, repeated or unknown identities. Source rows work with the existing hosted corpus partitioner, keeping a source’s queries together. Public root VIAL examples require exact version registrations; separate runtime-qualification fixtures are outside this supported-source cohort. The actual-query regression uses FSM::Test::SourceQueryRunner to invoke native JSON commands, the public in-process MCP adapter and a real newline stdio process. VIAL also passes through its explicit public filesystem API. It compares complete reports and text/structured payloads, and checks source/module identity, schema, adapter provenance, source hashes and repository-bound producer hashes. Normalization removes only the current repository prefix, including prefixes in diagnostic text; it never drops report fields or diagnostic entries. ISF schedule reports name a scheduled FSM artifact; IAL2 protocol reports have their own named schemas and source-object provenance. They do not share a universal wrapper.

Generated HDL size remains part of generation_result_snapshot.summary and is included in those comparisons. Expression sharing preserves ordered operands: (concat A A) and (concat B B) cannot share a driver merely because both are concatenations. Literal widths and radices, signal slices and aggregate paths also distinguish expressions. Expression kinds without a complete structural identity remain inline, including expressions that contain them. Candidate names are allocated deterministically. This prevents false sharing without removing size metadata or hiding differences between native and MCP reports. Complete response comparisons use canonical UTF-8 JSON hashes to keep failure diagnostics bounded; structured comparisons still identify differing fields.

Run the focused representative band, or select exact source identities:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/1884-semantic-source-query-runner.t t/1885-semantic-source-query-oracles.t
FSMGEN_SOURCE_QUERY_SOURCES='["isf/storage_fields.isf","vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial"]' scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl t/1884-semantic-source-query-runner.t

The default is a focused band. FSMGEN_SOURCE_QUERY_ALL=1 explicitly selects the full cohort and cannot be combined with a source filter. Hosted corpus shard selectors partition the selected source rows before execution, keeping all queries for each source together. This command lists the full query selection without executing a producer:

FSMGEN_SOURCE_QUERY_ALL=1 FSMGEN_HOSTED_CORPUS_LIST_ONLY=1 perl -Iperl t/1884-semantic-source-query-runner.t

For an execution receipt, set FSMGEN_SOURCE_QUERY_RECEIPT to a simple JSON basename. The existing repository-local .artifacts/mcp-feature-coverage/ directory receives selected identities, per-query report/source/producer hashes and the test pass state. A source requiring extra search paths fails explicitly until MCP has a corresponding public contract; such paths are never discarded.

The independent SourceQueryOracle checks authored ISF field ranges, access, reset and enum metadata; passive observation roles, signal order, widths and timing; hardware module/source identity; and VIAL actions, expressions, model instances, fault bindings, lifecycle prerequisites, deadlines and cleanup policy. These expectations come from authored fixtures and public contracts. T1885 deliberately gives every transport identical corrupted reports: parity still passes, but the independent oracle rejects missing or altered detail, incorrect scalar types, unknown families/revisions and wrong schema or provenance. Representative native hardware and VIAL refusals preserve their complete diagnostics through actual newline MCP, with isError and no partial success. These negative cases remain outside the supported-source cohort.

T1884 has its own hosted corpus partitions and is excluded from ordinary file shards. T1885 remains bounded ordinary regression. Local full regression and hosted T1884 dispatch force FSMGEN_SOURCE_QUERY_ALL=1; they reject ambient source filters, corpus list-only mode or shard coordinates before any command runs. Use direct prove for a focused developer run. Inspect CI dispatch without running the cohort:

./bin/ci-regression full --no-book --hosted-corpus-shard 1884:0/16 --dry-run

Focused transport parity and these selected feature witnesses are qualified; the exhaustive run remains separately tracked. Selection alone proves accounting; independent witnesses cover named semantics, not every possible meaning in every report. Catalog entries for plans, backends or runtime retain their identities here but source inspection does not execute or qualify those operations.

Before closing a public source-feature task, record its supported corpus identity, explicit source/version/query applicability, clean public API and corresponding MCP route in the owning task. Add a source case when existing cases do not cover the feature. Existing VIAL Summary Queries

Select language_version: 2 explicitly for VIAL v2, including the implemented lifecycle-control family. Omission selects v1; the adapter never guesses from the filename. Version selectors are rejected on hardware queries, and VIAL does not support schedule preview. These summary-query arguments are closed to source_id, its source_path alias, and the applicable language_version. Invalid selectors or inapplicable query kinds return JSON-RPC invalid params; source validation failures retain the public report and set tool isError.

perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":21,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"fsmgen_capability_query","arguments":{"section":"vial_tooling_v2"}}}'
perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":22,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"fsmgen_discover_sources","arguments":{"file_kind":"vial","limit":5}}}'

perl bin/fsmgen-mcp --workspace-root . --request-json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":24,"method":"resources/read","params":{"uri":"fsmgen://vial/2/source/vial/ahb_subordinate_base_output_arbitration_lifecycle_v2.vial/semantic"}}'

Capability-query sections vial_tooling_v1 and vial_tooling_v2 preserve the corresponding public capability records. The matching resource is fsmgen://vial/{language_version}/capabilities. Versioned source resources end in /check or /semantic; existing unversioned source resources also accept VIAL and default to v1. URI source identities may percent-encode /. Capabilities describe native tooling availability; a native plan capability does not advertise an MCP planning tool.

The caller-approved workspace bounds VIAL sources and imports. The public API rejects symlink components and off-volume files and enforces source/import loading limits; see the filesystem API contract. MCP preserves semantic paths such as /action as semantic identities, rather than treating them as host filesystem paths. Provenance names api_entrypoint and the selected language version; command_shape is null because no hardware CLI command is invoked. Feature coverage still requires actual feature-level qualification; discovery alone is not a semantic or runtime support claim.
